title: Node Nexus
tagline: Decentralized local WebOps agents using Gensyn AXL with 0G payments, inference, and storage.
description: Current WebOps is broken in two ways: it either depends on centralized data centers that do not reflect real world usage, or it depends on manual local testing that is too expensive and too slow to scale. Dev Teams miss what users actually see across regions, including pricing, consent banners, redirects, search results, blocked content, and login friction. Node Nexus solves this with a decentralized network of real user operated nodes communicating directly over Gensyn AXL. Operators set up a local node, connect it to AXL, publish their location, capabilities, and 0G payment address, then earn per task payments for providing real geographic coverage and execution capacity. 0G is used for payments, AI inference, and storage, while each node runs tasks locally, captures evidence, generates reports, stores and share them over 0G Storage.
how_its_made:
Node Nexus is built as a decentralized inter node system with a Node.js and Express coordination layer, a Next.js frontend, and a Python execution agent. Gensyn AXL is the core communication layer: nodes discover peers, exchange profile metadata, send node_nexus.execute tasks, and return async reports across separate AXL nodes without relying on any centralized broker. On each operator node, a Python agent uses browser-use and Playwright to perform browser tasks in the node’s real local environment. 

For AI inference, we use Qwen through the 0G OpenAI compatible router to help with execution and report analysis. We use 0G in three ways: direct per node task payments verified on 0G Galileo with ethers, AI inference through the 0G router, and durable report and metadata uploads to 0G Storage. This lets operators contribute useful local execution and get paid, while requesters get trustworthy real world web evidence instead of cloud region approximations.
